# `silk/crypto/curve448`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Agree on a shared secret with X448 (RFC 7748) on the Goldilocks curve, Curve448.

## When to use
Use [`X448`](#X448) when two parties must get the same secret over a channel that others can read and
a 224-bit security level is wanted, for example in a TLS 1.3 handshake with the `x448` group.
Each side makes a key with [`X448.generate`](#X448.impl.generate), sends [`X448.publicKey`](#X448.impl.publicKey), and calls
[`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) with the public key of the other side. Then derive the real keys from the shared
secret with `silk.crypto.hkdf`. For the more common 128-bit level, use `silk.crypto.x25519`.

## Details
Secrets, public keys, and shared secrets are 56 bytes, little-endian. A secret is clamped as RFC
7748 says, so all 56-byte values are valid. The field is the integers modulo
`p = 2^448 - 2^224 - 1`, held as eight 56-bit limbs, and every step on a secret runs in
constant time. Nothing allocates. Use `silk.crypto.okp_key` to read and write the keys in PKCS #8
and SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

## Errors
- [`X448Error`](#X448Error) for an input with the wrong length, or for a peer key that gives an all-zero
  secret.

## Gotchas
The exchange does not tell you who the other side is. An attacker in the middle can run one
exchange with each side. Authenticate the exchange, for example with a certificate signature. Do
not use the shared secret directly as a key. The key is not erased when it is dropped.

<a id="X448"></a>

## `X448`

```silk
pub struct X448
```

An X448 key pair: a secret and its public key.

### When to use
Use it when two parties must get the same secret over a channel that others can read. Each side
makes a key with [`X448.generate`](#X448.impl.generate), sends [`X448.publicKey`](#X448.impl.publicKey), and calls [`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) with the
public key of the other side.

### Details
[`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) consumes it; [`X448.agreeWith`](#X448.impl.agreeWith) borrows it, for a static key. Secrets, public
keys, and shared secrets are 56 bytes, little-endian. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas
The exchange does not tell you who the other side is. Authenticate the exchange, for example
with a certificate signature. Derive the real keys from the shared secret with
`silk.crypto.hkdf`. The key is not erased when it is dropped.

<a id="X448.impl.fromSecret"></a>

### Associated function `fromSecret`

```silk
pub fn fromSecret(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<X448, X448Error>
```

Returns the key pair for the 56-byte secret `bytes`. The bytes are copied, and clamped as RFC
7748 says before use.

#### Errors
- `InvalidScalarLength` if `bytes` is not 56 bytes.

#### Gotchas
For a new exchange, use [`X448.generate`](#X448.impl.generate). A secret that is used for two exchanges gives the
same public key to both, so the exchanges can be linked.

<a id="X448.impl.generate"></a>

### Associated function `generate`

```silk
pub effect fn generate() -> X448 ? &mut Random
```

Returns a new key pair with a secret from 56 bytes of the ambient `Random`.

The `Random` provider must be cryptographically secure. If it fails, the program stops. There
is no fallback to a weaker source.

<a id="X448.impl.secret"></a>

### Method `secret`

```silk
pub fn secret(self: &X448) -> [u8; 56]
```

Returns the 56 secret bytes as they were given, before clamping. PKCS #8 stores these bytes.

<a id="X448.impl.publicKey"></a>

### Method `publicKey`

```silk
pub fn publicKey(self: &X448) -> [u8; 56]
```

Returns the 56-byte public key to send to the peer. It does not consume the key pair.

<a id="X448.impl.agree"></a>

### Method `agree`

```silk
pub fn agree(self: X448, peer: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>
```

Returns the 56-byte shared secret for the public key `peer` of the other side, and consumes
the key pair.

As RFC 7748 says, any 56-byte value is accepted, also a value that is not below `p` or a point
that is not on the curve.

#### Errors
- `InvalidPeerLength` if `peer` is not 56 bytes.
- `AllZeroSharedSecret` if the result is all zeros. Stop the exchange.

The key pair is consumed also when it fails.

<a id="X448.impl.agreeWith"></a>

### Method `agreeWith`

```silk
pub fn agreeWith(self: &X448, peer: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>
```

Returns the 56-byte shared secret for the public key `peer`, as [`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) does, but
borrows the key pair so that a static key can agree with many peers.

#### Errors
- `InvalidPeerLength` if `peer` is not 56 bytes.
- `AllZeroSharedSecret` if the result is all zeros. Stop the exchange.

#### Gotchas
A static key gives no forward secrecy. Prefer a new key pair for each exchange.
